title: Benchmark IFC/BIM semantic interoperability with IfcOpenShell
objective: Produce reproducible evidence that the current IFC/BIM interoperability candidate (IfcOpenShell) can preserve and manipulate construction semantics across import, edit, export and round-trip workflows — IFC fixture, semantic extraction, controlled mutation, export, re-import, semantic comparison and Construction Graph mapping — without making the IFC library or engine-native model the canonical Construction Graph. IDS validation exercised with the IfcTester toolchain; BCF tested only if the toolchain supports it without material custom implementation.
acceptance_criteria: At least one representative IFC fixture completes import -> semantic extraction -> controlled mutation -> export -> re-import.
Semantic assertions prove which identities, classes, relationships, properties, quantities, units, and placements survive the round trip.
At least one deliberate mutation is shown to update the intended semantic object without silently altering unrelated objects.
Geometry-related round-trip assertions are explicit about what is and is not guaranteed.
The mapping into the Construction Graph is documented and reproducible, including provenance and unsupported-field handling.
Any lossy conversion or schema limitation is visible in the evidence report.
Results support, reject, or defer the candidate under the frozen adapter architecture.
non_goals: No decision that IFC is the complete internal representation for all ConstructionOS workflows.
No replacement of the Construction Graph with IFC entities.
No final legal approval based solely on this issue.
risk_assumptions: BCF toolchain limitation (probed, recorded as evidence): no installable BCF library exists in this environment — the PyPI 'bcf' distribution is unrelated firmware tooling (ftdi/flasher modules), and ifcopenshell 0.8.x does not bundle an ifcopenshell.bcf module. Issue #3 makes BCF conditional on toolchain support without material custom implementation, so BCF remains untested and is recorded as a limitation, not an engine failure.
IDS toolchain: IfcTester 0.8.5 (pip-installable, ifcopenshell-affiliated) provides IDS authoring and validation and is used in-process.

The ifcopenshell-ids 0.8.0 PyPI distribution is a broken partial mirror of ifcopenshell 0.8.0 with no ids module (wheel inspection evidence); it corrupts a co-installed ifcopenshell 0.8.5 and is NOT used.

spec/work-items.md still carries the older RESEARCH-CAD-003 definition (CAD-to-Construction-Graph prototype, RESEARCH-CAD-004 in the issue numbering); this record follows the GitHub issue #3 definition per the established divergence flag.
evidence_requirements: Deterministic pipeline benchmark: fixture -> extraction -> controlled mutation -> export -> re-import -> semantic comparison -> Construction Graph mapping.
Semantic assertions for identity, IFC class, relationships, properties, quantities, units, placements and supported geometry invariants.
Narrow-patch mutation proof with lineage recording.
Construction Graph mapping proof with engine-id non-canonicality, provenance and explicit lossy/unsupported/inferred/opaque-lineage classification.
IDS validation workflow (positive and negative controls); BCF toolchain probe evidence.
Exact IfcOpenShell/IfcTester/schema/runtime versions recorded; runtime and output-size measurements.

decisions.rationale: PR #19's IFC/BIM evidence is substantially strong and the research workflow is green, but approval is blocked by the governance inconsistency introduced by the Architecture v1.1 (ACR-002) merge: architecture-versions.json is active 1.1 while protected-paths.json still targets 1.0. The failure originates from the ACR-002 merge, not this work item. No architecture change is requested for the IFC semantic layer; Architecture v1.1 remains active but the governance consistency defect must be corrected before this work item can proceed to approval.
decisions.remediation_required: 1) Repair the manifest/registry consistency in a focused architecture-governance PR (do not weaken or bypass the check), then rebase PR #19 and rerun governance. 2) Preserve the work-item version: RESEARCH-CAD-003 retains Architecture v1.0 unless its implementation genuinely depends on v1.1. 3) Keep the IDS/BCF findings explicit, including the broken ifcopenshell-ids mirror and the unrelated PyPI bcf package as toolchain findings, not architectural blockers. 4) Do not claim final IFC/BIM verification until the governance defect is cleared and the corrected PR is revalidated.
